column1: # boru Language Specification: boru:fn-util — the point-free function
# vocabulary (FnUtil namespace)
# Format: input<TAB>expected<TAB>description
# The module ships the audit's §6.4 recommendation
# (design/HIGHER-ORDER-FUNCTIONS.0.md): compose, pipe, curry, partial,
# const, identity, flip, on, memoize. Only the rows that COMPILE live
# here (the main corpus holds refusalCeiling = 0); the behaviour rows
# def-bind a computed fn — "def-bound computed fn apply (closure shape
# unknown — Stage 1)", the §5.4 / NUR101 family — so they live in
# lang/spec/frontier/frontier-fn-util.tsv until that family graduates.
import "boru:fn-util"  FnUtil.identity 42
import "boru:fn-util"  FnUtil.identity 'v'
# The REFUSAL rows compile: curry's shape checks run inside the native,
# on an operand the recorder now bakes as an inert const (the family's
# CompileStoresFn declaration), so the compiled lane raises the same
# type_error the interpreter does. The BEHAVIOUR rows still cannot —
# they def-bind the computed fn, which is the second wall (§5.4 /
# NUR101) — and stay in the frontier ledger.
import "boru:fn-util"  def f fn [a:Integer Integer [a] s:String String [s]] end def c (FnUtil.curry f/v)
